newsitem.title: USA: CME lumber closes sharply lower on profit taking.
newsitem.headline: CME lumber closes sharply lower on profit taking.

text.p: Profit taking after the recent sharp runup in values weighed on CME lumber futures with prices ending sharply lower on reports cash lumber trade had also slowed, traders said.

July, November and distant January fell as much as the daily limit of $10.00 per thousand board feet early before ending sharply lower. Futures finished $4.80 to $9.20 per tbf lower with May off the least at $406.70 and July off most at $393.60.
The market looked overbought despite soaring cash lumber quotes as cash trade reportedly slowed, financials tumbled and poor weather cut demand in some areas, traders said.
May futures had posted limit gains of $10.00 on Tuesday and Wednesday and an expanded limit of $15.00 on Thursday.
"Wholesalers got into the game yesterday and decided to buy some wood so the pipeline's probably close to full right now," said Neil Schmaedick, Smith Barney Forest Products analyst.

However, Schmaedick noted that the cash market remains strong. Mills have order files out two to three weeks and may still raise asking prices to see if there are any takers at the higher values, he said.

Random Lengths quoted cash spruce at $407 per tbf Friday, up $13 from midweek and $27 above last Friday. The Random Lengths Framing Lumber Composite price rose $14, to its highest level since November, Random Lengths reported.

Cash lumber prices have jumped $40 from its recent low on March 26. Many dealers and wholesales had kept stocks low in anticipation of a huge supply of wood coming from Canada at the start ot the new quota year, April 1. However, the wood did not show up and demand rose as warm weather spread across much of the nation, analysts said.
